audit.whatIsWrong: win[2], win[3] and win[4] said Tahm Kench / Skill / Skill while the page's own whys call Level 3 'your full Q-W combo lands', Levels 4-5 'your tank lane-control peak' and Level 6 'your cleanest 1v1 kill window'. The packet chart has K'Sante for all three.
audit.why: Tahm has no dash — Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 — so the levels where K'Sante has W and E up are his, and Tahm's value returns on items.
audit.corrected: Level 3, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 all flipped to K'Sante at 6/10, in matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Lvl 2-3, Lvl 6, first item, late are the right beats.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ability slots were wrong throughout. Devour is R, not W ('his W devour' appears five times); W is Abyssal Dive, a dive and knockup with no percent-health component, so 'his percent-HP W' is invented; and 'grey-health passive' conflates Thick Skin (E, the stored-damage shield) with An Acquired Taste (P, the stack counter that scales his damage off his own health). Tongue Lash's stun was also written as unconditional — it only stuns at three An Acquired Taste stacks.
audit.why: The stack condition is the whole early lane: you can count his damage instances and know exactly when the stun is live. And Thick Skin banks the chip you deal and cashes it as a shield, which is why a poke war loses and a single committed trade wins.
audit.corrected: Slots corrected everywhere, the three-stack condition stated, Thick Skin named as the shield, and the invented percent-HP W removed.
sources: mirrorFindings point 4 (three stacks buys exactly one of the two)

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole content layer is written in first person ('I', 'me', 'my'), and mid claims 'he has no dash to escape my R recall'.
audit.why: The site's voice is second person, and K'Sante's R has no recall — it launches the target through a wall and dashes after them.
audit.corrected: All of early, mid, late, spikes and wants rewritten in second person; the recall claim removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither missing interaction reached the content layer: Thick Skin and Devour both absorb your burst, and his Tongue Lash/Thick Skin sustain needs Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Committing into a full Thick Skin bar wastes the trade; the shield has to be forced out first.
audit.corrected: Written into mid, late, whys[6] and wants.foe[1].

edits.before: Tahm Kench's whole early threat is his Q tongue — it stuns me at range and sets up his W devour or a roam, so I keep my E Footwork ready to dash over the wall or to a minion and deny the lash. At Level 1 I only have Q with no engage, so I just farm and don't walk into tongue range. The catch on him: his grey-health passive refills any chip I do with Q poke, so I'm not winning a poke war — I'm waiting for my Level 3 combo to land a real knockup trade he can't grey-heal away.
edits.after: Tahm Kench's whole early threat is Tongue Lash — 900 range, it heals him and stacks An Acquired Taste, and only the third stack stuns, so count his hits. Keep E Footwork ready to dash to a minion and break the lash line. At Level 1 you only have Q with no engage, so just farm outside tongue range. The catch: Thick Skin banks the chip your Q poke deals and cashes it as a shield, so you are not winning a poke war — wait for the Level 3 combo and take one real trade.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are my lane-control window. With Q-W online I bait his Q tongue, then W-charge an overcommitted Tahm and Q3 him for a knockup that does real damage before his grey-health refills — this is where I bank small leads as a tank. At 6, All Out is my best shot: it strips my bulk but turns me into a duelist who can dash through his slow, low-mobility body and actually kill him, since he has no dash to escape my R recall. Don't ult into full grey-health, though — bait his W devour and passive first, then commit.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are your lane-control window. With Q-W online you bait Tongue Lash, then W an overcommitted Tahm for the knockback-stun and Q3-pull him, doing real damage before Thick Skin converts it — this is where you bank small leads as a tank. At 6, All Out is your best shot: it strips your bulk but turns you into a duelist who runs his slow body down, since Abyssal Dive is 21 seconds and it is his only exit. Don't commit into a full Thick Skin bar — force the shield out first, then go.

edits.before: This is where Tahm reclaims it and the 47.5% shows. His W devour does percent-HP and his grey-health passive out-lasts every bit of damage my armor-stacked tank profile can output, so my late-game scaling does nothing against him — I can't burst through regen and I can't out-sustain a drain tank. Worse, his R map roams snowball other lanes while I'm stuck top. My only path is to have already banked a lead on my 3-6 windows, then group and use R to peel him off my carries in teamfights rather than trying to solo-duel a percent-HP sustain monster.
edits.after: This is where Tahm reclaims it and the 47.5% shows. An Acquired Taste scales his damage off his own health and Thick Skin banks every bit of damage your armour-stacked profile outputs, so without Grievous Wounds you cannot burst through him and cannot out-sustain him. Worse, Devour shields a teammate out of a fight you are not even in. Your path is to bank a lead on the 3-6 windows, then group and use R to launch him off your carries rather than solo-duelling a sustain tank.

notes: This matchup's content layer was written in first person throughout — every 'I/me/my' is now second person. Devour was called W in five places (it is R), Abyssal Dive was credited with percent-health damage it does not have, and 'grey-health passive' merged Thick Skin (E) with An Acquired Taste (P). The three-stack condition on Tongue Lash's stun is now stated, which matches the mirror's finding that three stacks buys exactly one of the stun or Devour.
